questions.prompt: Granted that the thief is wicked, he will never escape the guards' hands.
questions.answer: Sit fūr improbus, numquam tamen manūs custōdum effugiet.

questions.prompt: I grant that the general was wounded, yet he refused to desert the battle-line.
questions.answer: Fuerit dux sauciātus, aciem tamen dēserere nōluit.

questions.prompt: I grant there is no strength in old age; yet counsel and reason survive.
questions.answer: Nē sint in senectūte vīrēs, cōnsilium tamen et ratiō supersunt.

questions.prompt: I grant the young lad was troublesome to others; when did he begin to be so to you?
questions.answer: Fuerit adulescentulus aliīs molestus; tibi quandō esse coepit?

questions.prompt: Grant that what you tell is true; it will still not move me.
questions.answer: Sit hoc vērum quod nārrās, mē tamen nōn movēbit.

questions.prompt: I grant the judge does not believe me; yet he will hear the witnesses themselves.
questions.answer: Nē crēdat mihi iūdex, testēs tamen ipsōs audiet.

questions.prompt: I grant that poet was once obscure; today he is praised by everyone.
questions.answer: Fuerit ille poēta obscūrus; hodiē tamen ab omnibus laudātur.

questions.prompt: Grant the freedwoman is poor; she nevertheless lives with a free spirit.
questions.answer: Sit liberta pauper, animō tamen līberō vīvit.

questions.prompt: I grant I possess no gold; yet I possess faithful friends.
questions.answer: Nē habeam aurum, amīcōs tamen fidēlēs possideō.

questions.prompt: I grant the enemy was cruel; yet at last he released the captives.
questions.answer: Fuerit hostis crūdēlis; captīvōs tamen tandem dīmīsit.

questions.prompt: Grant the road is long and steep through the mountains; I will still lead you.
questions.answer: Sit via longa et per montēs ardua, tē tamen dūcam.

questions.prompt: I grant the orator does not win by his skill; yet he prevails by his cause.
questions.answer: Nē vincat orātor arte, causā tamen superat.

questions.prompt: I grant the slave was once a runaway; now he serves his master most faithfully.
questions.answer: Fuerit servus fugitīvus; nunc tamen dominō fidēlissimē servit.

questions.prompt: Grant the storm is savage; the sailors will still not furl the sails.
questions.answer: Sit tempestās atrōx, nautae tamen vēla nōn contrahent.

questions.prompt: I grant you have no money; yet you have talent and shrewdness.
questions.answer: Nē sit tibi pecūnia, ingenium tamen et acūmen habēs.

questions.prompt: I grant that fellow was a wicked citizen to many; yet to me he was always useful.
questions.answer: Fuerit iste cīvis improbus multīs; mihi tamen semper prōfuit.

questions.prompt: Grant the field is barren and full of stones; the farmer does not give up.
questions.answer: Sit ager sterilis et saxīs plēnus, colōnus tamen nōn dēsistit.

questions.prompt: I grant the boy does not understand the Greek words; yet he imitates the sound.
questions.answer: Nē intellegat puer verba Graeca, sonum tamen imitātur.

questions.prompt: I grant the king was proud; yet he magnificently built the temples of the gods.
questions.answer: Fuerit rēx superbus; templa tamen deōrum magnificē exstrūxit.

questions.prompt: Grant the winter is cold and bristling with snows; the soldiers still advance.
questions.answer: Sit hiems frīgida et nivibus horrida, mīlitēs tamen prōgrediuntur.

questions.prompt: I grant the gods do not favor my undertakings; I will dare nonetheless.
questions.answer: Nē faveant dī coeptīs, ego tamen audēbō.

questions.prompt: I grant the young man was foolish; yet he turned out a serious fellow.
questions.answer: Fuerit adulēscēns ineptus; vir tamen gravis ēvāsit.

questions.prompt: Grant the gift is small; yet the spirit of the giver is great.
questions.answer: Sit dōnum parvum, animus tamen dantis magnus est.

questions.prompt: I grant you have not believed me; the facts themselves will speak.
questions.answer: Nē mihi crēdiderīs; rēs tamen ipsae loquentur.
